item.description: model: add Muse Spark Open (text, vision and audio) (#30616) * model: add Muse Spark Open (text, vision and audio) Muse Spark Open is a latent space MoE: the residual stream stays at 8192 while the 256 experts live in 4096, with a projection down and up around them, top-8 sigmoid routing with a correction bias. Attention interleaves three sliding layers at a 2048 window with rope for one global layer without rope, with a sigmoid output gate and a weightless QK-norm. Residuals are norm preserving, their gate is folded at conversion time. Vision reuses the Muse Glimmer tower. Audio is a causal convolutional pyramid with no attention and no spectrogram, four stages folding 16, 6, 5 and 4 samples into the channel dim, one embedding per 80 ms of 24 kHz. The quantizer keeps the latent projections and the attention gate at Q8_0, a little over 1% of the weights, since the whole residual stream passes through them and the low-bit types turned the output into a repeating loop. The model saver writes the post norm epsilon, and the arch is registered in test-llama-archs. item.description: ## Overview llama.cpp v0.7.0 adds the LiliCorr speculative decoding technique and MTP for GLM5-Next, a new GPU cache for MoE experts kept in host memory (--moe-cache-mib, up to ~2.2x decode speedup when experts are offloaded), and a large batch of new models: K2 Horizon (dense and MoVA), Prism Bonsai 2 27B, EmbeddingGemma-2 (text+vision+audio), the LiquidAI d1/d1-omni and vLLM decision 2/d3 decision models, pplx-decider, MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL / Nemotron Bolt and maion-coder. The server gets a refactored chat session API (common_chat_session, part-based formatted output), much better slot and prompt-cache restore behavior, decision-model support for the new architectures and a new default port (9931), the web UI gains a full models manager, and ggml is updated to v0.27.0. ### Highlights - GLM5-Next: MTP speculative decoding with an optimized sparse attention path #29928 - K2 Horizon support in both dense and MoVA variants: conversion, tokenizer, chat template, -sm tensor splitting #29535 - Prism Bonsai 2 27B ternary model support #29600 - EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embedding model #30054 - New decision models: LiquidAI d1-3B, d1-omni-600M, vLLM decision 2, vLLM d3 and pplx-decider #30110 #30114 #30378 #30383 #30044 - PLaMo-3 tokenizer implements reference pre-segmentation for exact tokenization parity #30045 - RPC server supports -sm tensor (tensor-parallel RPC, RPC protocol v8) #26610 - Server now listens on port 9931 by default instead of 8080 #30159 ### API changes - include/llama.h: new moe_cache_size context param for the host-expert GPU cache #29887 - include/llama.h: new LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_PLAMO3 vocab type #30045 - include/llama.h: llama_perf_context_data reports graph reallocations during inference #30329 - include/llama.h: embeddings now skips the LM head when a pooling type other than NONE is used #30445 - include/llama.h: llama_batch_ext_set_embd_state returns false when the context has no state embedding, M-RoPE order documented #30506 - tools/server: chat layer refactored around common_chat_session with feed() / finish() #30210 - tools/server: formatted chat output is now an array of parts instead of a single string #30389 - tools/server: default listening port changed to 9931 (Docker images keep 8080 inside the container) #30159 ### New models - K2 Horizon: dense and MoVA variants with conversion, tokenizer, chat template and -sm tensor support #29535 - Prism Bonsai 2 27B (ternary) #29600 - EmbeddingGemma-2: text + vision + audio embeddings #30054 - LiquidAI d1-3B and d1-omni-600M decision models #30110 #30114 - vLLM decision 2 and vLLM d3 models #30378 #30383 - pplx-decider decision model #30044 - MiniCPM-V 4.7 multimodal model #29416 - Nemotron Super 3.5 VL and Nemotron Bolt 74B A9B #30520 - Speculative decoding: MTP for GLM5-Next, LiliCorr drafts, correct mtmd handling in MTP graphs #29928 #30506 #30257 - Speculative decoding: shared nextn tensor flags with consolidated row cropping and sched re-reserve on flag change #30097 #30017 #30020 - MoE expert cache: host-memory experts served from a device LRU cache, supported over multiple GPUs #29887 #30112 - Embedding models: skip the logits buffer and the LM head when pooling is enabled (up to 10x less VRAM) #30255 #30445 - Embedding graphs: reordered get_rows, dropped the redundant t_embd expand and leftover ggml_cont calls #30160 #30461 #30198 - No-cache attention: padded KV dimension and KQ bias, avoided graph reallocations #30416 #30446 #30439 - Prefetching: merge ranges before issuing system prefetch calls, never map foreign ranges into a backend buffer #30532 #30405 - Sampling: greedy selection for eligible temperature-zero chains, backend sampling graph kept static across ubatches #29797 #30223 - Model split: distribute layers evenly when no device reports free memory #29677 ### Multi-modality changes - Added mtmd_build_inp_attn_mask for building non-causal multimodal attention masks #30259 - Added cohere2 vision encoder support #30062 - MTP drafts now handle mtmd inputs, Qwen3.8 Flash Next accepts image embeddings #30257 #30397 - New multimodal architectures: MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL, EmbeddingGemma-2 (vision + audio) #29416 #30520 #30054 ### Server changes - Generated text and tokens are now accumulated as parser input, preparing token-aware parsing #29876 - Prompt cache: only restorable slot states are saved, so rerank and embedding requests no longer fill the cache #30498 - Prompt cache: child tasks prefer empty slots and preserve the state they would overwrite #30567 - A pinned busy slot is left untouched until the request can run on it #30295 - Slot save/restore now keeps context checkpoints and the draft model state #26004 #30574 - Fixed an off-by-two in the SWA reuse threshold that discarded restored states #30580 - Fixed a stack-overflow crash when escaping special tokens with std::regex #30243 - LLAMA_ARG_SLOT_SAVE_PATH environment variable for --slot-save-path #30272 - New per-component server tests; vendored cpp-httplib updated to 0.61.0 #30312 #30494 #30134 #30081 ### UI changes - New Models Manager: one table of all served models with expandable quants, search, filters, sorting and favorites #29583 - Row actions: load/unload, delete from disk, hide/unhide, resumable downloads with progress #29583 - Model configuration side drawer with model info, chat template and "start a new chat" / "use in this chat" actions #29583 - Models manager follow-ups: GGUF training context, favorite UX, filter and sort fixes #30228 - Fixed ui_settings not being applied on the first visit in router mode #29668 - Fixed text attachment preview overflow for large pasted text #29898 - Fixed the default agentic turns limit falling back to 10 instead of 100 #30582 ### ggml changes - ggml updated to v0.27.0: the backend scheduler gains user callbacks for split weight copying and compute-buffer reallocation, and the RPC protocol is bumped to v8 for tensor-parallel RPC servers. Backends gained chunked gated-delta-net kernels on CUDA/HIP, KleidiAI SME2 k-quant matmuls and AVX2 Q2_0 dot products on CPU, L2-aware coopmat2 scheduling and bf16 activations on Vulkan, reordered-layout MoE kernels (MXFP4, IQ3, Q5_K, grouped XMX GEMM) on SYCL, dp4a MoE GEMMs on OpenCL, tensor-API and wider-head-dim flash attention on Metal, and a DMA/HVX copy overhaul with pooling and 3D im2col ops on Hexagon. Correctness work focused on non-contiguous and strided views, grid and workgroup size limits, out-of-bounds accesses and well-defined mul_mat_id behavior for duplicate expert ids; symbol visibility item.description: server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache (#30498) * server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache The idle-slot save loop stores every idle slot whenever a task starts, while only completion tasks restore from the prompt cache. Rerank, embedding, decision and infill states fill the cache up to its limit without ever being read back, and slots already cached are offered again at every task start. Each slot now tracks with cache_pending whether its state is restorable and missing from the cache: a completion release or an explicit slot restore sets it, prompt_save consumes it, prompt_clear resets it. Both save paths share this rule, and the LRU path restores only for completion tasks. * server: test that decision slots skip the prompt cache Decision tasks never mark their slot as cacheable, so starting new tasks must not save their idle slots to the RAM prompt cache, with or without a unified KV cache. * server: restore any reusing task from the prompt cache Embedding and rerank tasks never reuse their state, so their slots are cleared on release like child slots and the cache only holds states that a later task can restore. Infill and decision tasks now restore from the cache too, which replaces the cache_pending flag. Decision models disable the prompt cache unless --cache-ram is given, since their states seldom repeat. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input (#28738) * ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input The GEMM behind conv_1d folds the batch into its rows, so the product sits in memory as [OL, N, OC] while the reshape claims [OL, OC, N]. The shape is right and the contents are transposed, so nothing fires: no assert, no abort, the graph just runs and the channels come out interleaved with the batches. With N == 1 the two readings describe the same buffer, which is why the three vocoders in the tree never hit it, they all squeeze to 2d right after the call. Reshape to the real layout and permute OC and N back. The N == 1 path keeps its direct reshape, so the current callers build the same graph and pay for no extra copy. tests/test-conv-1d.cpp compares one batched convolution against N single batch convolutions built from the same weight and the same input slices. Five of the seven geometries fail before this change and all seven pass after. N == 1 and OC == 1 pass either way, since swapping two dimensions when one of them is 1 changes nothing. The batched path matters to downstream audio projects where several synthesis lanes share a single graph. Nothing in mtmd batches a vocoder today, each one streams one flow and carries its left context between calls, but the op is correct now if one of them grows a lane dimension. * ggml: build the same conv_1d graph for every batch size Address review from ggerganov: drop the N == 1 branch of ggml_conv_1d. The GEMM result is always reshaped to [OC, N, OL] and permuted back, as ggml_conv_2d does, so every batch size builds the same graph. For N == 1 this adds a cont on an already ordered tensor. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings (#30445) * graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings A context that extracts pooled embeddings outputs one vector per sequence, but every model still expanded its LM head, so the graph computed n_vocab logits per token and the context kept a host buffer for them. The models now only declare t_logits, and set_outputs() expands it unless the context extracts embeddings with a pooling type other than NONE. Since the toggle changes the graph shape for a pooled context, set_embeddings() schedules a re-reserve in that case. * graph: drop the redundant t_embd expand Address review from @CISC: with embeddings on, build_pooling() already expands its output for every pooling type, and a decoder graph without embeddings does not read t_embd, so set_outputs() only expands t_logits. * graph: add build_logits() for the LM head output Address review from @ggerganov: the LM head is expanded by a dedicated build_logits(), called from llama_model::build_graph() like build_pooling(), and set_outputs() only marks the outputs again. * graph: call build_logits() before build_sampling() Address review from @ggerganov: build_sampling() reads t_logits, so the LM head is built first. A pooled context then skips the sampling layers too, since it has no logits to sample from. * nit **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: tests : consolidate context state tests into test-llama-context (#30023) * tests : consolidate the context state tests into test-llama-context test-save-load-state, test-recurrent-state-rollback and test-state-restore-fragmented check the same object from three places: the KV cache and the recurrent state of a llama_context, saved, loaded, copied, rolled back. Each had its own main, its own loop over the models, its own copy of the token and the comparison helpers, and a run of all three loaded the same models several times. They are one binary now, and the case is the unit of the test: tests/llama-context/test-case.h the interface a case implements tests/llama-context/cases-kv.cpp the cases of the KV cache tests/llama-context/cases-rs.cpp the cases of the recurrent state tests/llama-context/test-util.cpp tokens, generation, comparison tests/llama-context/test-runner.cpp the models of a case, on threads tests/llama-context/test-log.cpp the log file of a model A run is a table: a row per model, a column per case, a cell holds the verdict of that pair. The models load on several threads (-j, --threads, min(cores, 4) by default), the table is printed when it is complete and the log of a model that failed is printed after it, in the order of the rows. A case returns a verdict and the reason for it, and the runner is the only one who reports - the test does not use tests/testing.h, a run over 130 models is a matrix of verdicts and not a tree of subtests. Staging no longer travels through the environment: llama_model_set_attn_rot replaces the LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE variable, which a model loaded in one thread used to change for the models the other threads were loading, and llama_memory_get_buffers is added for the cases that copy the buffers of a memory. common_log_set_stdo keeps the console quiet while the table is being built. ggml_aligned_malloc allocates with posix_memalign when the thread sanitizer is on. On macOS it allocates with the Mach VM, which the sanitizer does not intercept, so it never sees a page range change hands and reports the first write into recycled memory as a race - 30 of them in this test, and every one of them false. item.description: graph: pad the KV dimension of the no-cache attention to 256 (#30416) The no-cache path builds a [n_tokens, n_tokens] mask and passes K and V unpadded, so FLASH_ATTN_EXT sees K->ne[1] == n_tokens. The CUDA kernels for head size 512 require a multiple of FATTN_KQ_STRIDE, so the op falls back to the CPU for most lengths, and the -fa auto probe (1 token) disables flash attention for such models. item.description: metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids (#30373) * metal : fix mul_mat_id limits and kernel name * metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 assumed at most one match per token and a fixed capacity of ne21 entries per expert, which produced wrong or dropped output rows and could overflow into the slice of the next expert when the ids contain duplicates. build a compact per-expert list of the (token, slot) entries instead: - pass 1 counts the entries of every expert, thread 0 computes the offsets of the expert slices (tpe now holds [base, count]) - pass 2 writes the entries with one unconditional store per token (conditional stores of divergent lanes are very slow), the dummy value of the tokens without a match lands on a padding slot of the slice that is never read - duplicates are handled by a rare branch - kernel_mul_mm_id reads the base/count of its expert and loops over the entry tiles that do not fit into the grid The ids buffer is sized as ne20*ne21 + ne02 (entries + padding). 883/883 test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID tests pass, llama-bench is within run-to-run variance of the previous behavior. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD * metal : make mul_mat_id map0 ne02 a function constant use FOR_UNROLL for the id loops of kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 and turn ne02 into the function constant FC_mul_mm_id_map0_ne02 (FC_MUL_MM + 7), so that the threadgroup offsets of cnt/bas/sids and the prefix-sum bound fold at compile time. the pipeline name now encodes ne02 (same convention as the ssm_conv nc/silu constants) and the map0 pipeline is compiled with the constant value set. ne02 is no longer part of ggml_metal_kargs_mul_mm_id_map0 - the dispatch grid still comes from the tensor ne[2] on the host. no measurable perf change: 883/883 test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID tests pass, op-level and llama-bench results are within run variance. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD * cont : clean-up + TODO * metal : dispatch mul_mat_id entry tiles from the prepass follow the approach of the vulkan implementation (#29998): instead of launching a grid over experts x ne21 entry tiles and letting most of the threadgroups early exit, kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 now also emits a row map - the total tile count plus one (expert, first entry, valid rows) descriptor per 32-entry tile that has work. kernel_mul_mm_id is launched with a static upper bound on the number of tiles (full tiles over all entries plus at most one partial tile per expert), reads its descriptor and processes a single tile - the tail early exits. This removes the round loop that was needed to cover duplicate ids past the grid (register pressure: th_max 768 -> back to the plain mul_mm level) and duplicates are now handled implicitly, since they only produce more descriptors within the bound. Non-numeric values fall back to 1. The duplicated env/macro blocks in ggml-rpc.cpp and transport.cpp are replaced by a shared log.h, which becomes the single choke point for all logging of the RPC backend: LOG_ERROR/LOG_WARN/LOG_INFO for unconditional severity logs and LOG_DBG/LOG_DBG2/LOG_DBG3 for the verbosity-gated ones. The transport files no longer need ggml-impl.h, and the server banner now also goes through the ggml logger (stderr). Missing logs are added on both the client (handshake, buffer ops, tensor transfers, graph computes, cache decisions) and the server (per-command dispatch, graph nodes), including the negotiated transport via the new socket_t::transport_name(). This fixes the assert hit by KV cache views when using --split-mode tensor with partial offload.
